question: What is the role of the hotel, accommodation, and hospitality industry in Uganda's economy?
answer: The hotel and accommodation sector is a core pillar of Uganda's services economy and the primary enabler of tourism, generating substantial foreign exchange and employment across accommodation, food service, recreation, and event hosting. Governed in partnership with the Uganda Hotel Owners Association (UHOA), operators range from luxury 5-star establishments to boutique lodges, guesthouses, and safari camps. Commercial operators must register with URSB, obtain operating licenses from the Uganda Tourism Board (UTB), acquire municipal trading licenses from KCCA or local town councils, and register with URA for tax obligations.

question: What is Local Hotel Tax (LHT) in Uganda, who pays it, and what are the applicable rates?
answer: Local Hotel Tax (LHT) is a local government levy paid by room occupants of hotels, lodges, and guesthouses per room per night. Hotel management collects the tax as a statutory pass-through and remits it monthly to KCCA or the local Municipal/Town Council. For income tax purposes, LHT is NOT recognized as hotel revenue and is NOT an allowable expense for the hotel owner. Statutory LHT rates: 1) Four and Five-Star Hotels: USD 2 per room per night; 2) Two and Three-Star Hotels and other hotels charging above UGX 50,000 per night: UGX 2,000 per room per night; 3) Hotels, lodges, and guesthouses charging UGX 10,000 to UGX 50,000 per night: UGX 1,000 per room per night; 4) Budget lodges and guesthouses charging below UGX 10,000 per night: UGX 500 per room per night.

question: What customs duty and tax exemptions are available for goods imported by licensed hotels in Uganda?
answer: Under the Fifth Schedule of the East African Community Customs Management Act (EACCMA 2004) Part B Item 21, goods engraved, printed, or permanently marked with the hotel logo imported by a licensed hotel for its exclusive use are exempt from all customs duties and taxes (0% import duty and VAT exempt): 1) Washing machines and clothes-dryers; 2) Kitchenware instruments, cookers, and cooking apparatus; 3) Refrigerators and freezers; 4) Air conditioning systems; 5) Cutlery and dining implements; 6) Televisions and audio-visual displays; 7) Carpets and textile floor coverings; 8) Hotel furniture (tables, chairs, beds); 9) Bed linen, sheets, pillowcases, duvet covers, and curtains; 10) Gymnasium and fitness equipment; 11) Battery-operated vehicles (golf carts and guest shuttles); 12) Bathrobes and clothes dryers enjoy 0% import duty (reduced from 25%) for one year.

question: What tax exemptions apply to tour operators and tourism transport equipment in Uganda?
answer: Under URA guidelines at https://ura.go.ug/en/tourism-sector-2/ and EACCMA Fifth Schedule Part B Item 21: 1) Specially modified 4x4 tourist motor vehicles imported by licensed tour operators (recommended by the Ministry of Tourism, Wildlife and Antiquities / UTB) are 100% exempt from import duty and VAT; 2) Sightseeing buses equipped with comfortable reclining coach seats, lavatory facilities, and first aid provisions are duty-free; 3) Overland safari trucks featuring high off-road ground clearance, reclining seats, electrical inverters, mobile kitchens, food storage, and camping tents are duty-free; 4) Tourism boats imported by licensed tour operators are exempt from all import taxes; 5) Tour operator packages and domestic air transport services are subject to specific VAT rules.

question: What tax obligations apply to restaurants, outside catering operators, and recreational facilities?
answer: Under URA guidelines at https://ura.go.ug/en/restaurant-and-outside-catering-operators/ and https://ura.go.ug/en/recreation-facilities/: 1) Standard taxes: 30% Corporation Tax on net business profits (or presumptive turnover tax for small operators with gross sales between UGX 10M and UGX 150M), PAYE on culinary and service staff, and 18% VAT; 2) Mandatory EFRIS: All restaurants, caterers, and recreation centers (golf courses, amusement parks, cinemas, gyms, camping sites) must issue fiscalized e-invoices/e-receipts through EFRIS for all food, beverage, and admission sales; 3) Withholding Tax: Corporate and government clients procuring outside catering services exceeding UGX 1,000,000 must withhold 6% WHT unless the catering vendor holds a valid WHT exemption certificate; 4) Input VAT Credit: While raw, unprocessed foodstuffs are VAT-exempt, caterers can claim input tax credit on commercial gas (LPG), packaging materials, kitchen equipment, and utility bills.

question: Where can I download the official URA Hotel and Accommodation Sector Taxation Guide?
answer: The official compendium 'A Guide to Taxation of the Hotel and Accommodation Sector' (Vol. 1 FY 2025-26, 40 pages, joint URA–UHOA publication) is downloadable at https://ura.go.ug/storage/2025/10/A-guide-to-taxation-of-the-Hotel-and-Accomodation-Sector-2025-26.pdf and published under URA Tax Education > Hospitality at https://ura.go.ug/en/category/tax-education/hospitality/hotels/. Additional subsector guides include Hotel & Accommodation (June 24, 2023 - 8:52 am, https://ura.go.ug/en/hotel-and-accommodation-sector/), Recreation Facilities (https://ura.go.ug/en/recreation-facilities/), Tourism Sector (https://ura.go.ug/en/tourism-sector-2/), Restaurant and Outside Catering Operators (https://ura.go.ug/en/restaurant-and-outside-catering-operators/), and Business Formalisation (January 25, 2024 - 10:32 am, https://ura.go.ug/en/business-formalisation/).
